clue.text: Language that's often assumed to be French

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the tongue spoken in Poland

definitions.text: that's often assumed to be French

explanation.surface: A remark about a tongue people tend to mistake for French.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the capital and the language becomes a finish: French polish is a traditional shellac finish for wood, so 'polish' is often followed by 'French'.
explanation.definitionFit: One spelling serves as the nationality adjective of Poland and as the glossy coating that commonly carries the qualifier French.

clue.text: Embezzle money once received by means of collection in church

indicators.note: something received is taken in, so the first piece sits inside the second

parts.note: the collection plate is passed round at a church service
the ecu was the European currency unit before the euro

explanation.surface: A churchwarden pocketing cash from the Sunday offering.
explanation.definitionFit: To peculate is to steal public or entrusted funds, a formal word for embezzlement.

clue.text: What's extended for catching sun when stripped?

definitions.text: What's extended for catching sun when stripped?

indicators.note: catching means holding, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: extended means made longer

indicators.note: stripping a word removes its outer layers, leaving only the middle letter

parts.note: the middle letter of sun once its outer letters are stripped

explanation.surface: A sunbed laid out flat for someone sunbathing in little or nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a sunbed, while extended, catching and sun-stripped build it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sun lounger is a reclining chair that lies flat by a pool or beach so people can sunbathe.

clue.text: Subversive issue, not new in South America

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the letters that follow

parts.note: S for South and US for America

indicators.note: not new tells you to drop the letter that stands for new

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a publication

explanation.surface: An insurgent newsletter circulating in South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Seditious speech or action incites rebellion against the state, which is what subversive means.

clue.text: Coastal path once rich in diversity

indicators.note: diversity means variety, so the letters are set out in a varied, different order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters

explanation.surface: A seaside walk that was once wealthy in its variety.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road or way cut along a coast or cliff face, as on the Riviera.

clue.text: Available to accept it as an alternative

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the outer phrase opens to hold another

parts.note: on hand means available
'it' and 'the other' are both coy British euphemisms for sex

explanation.surface: Someone ready to take on a task as a substitute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of the other' is British slang for sex, as is 'it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a contrasting option, offering another way of looking at things.

clue.text: Lowest point of delta overwhelmed by pouring rain

indicators.note: being overwhelmed means being engulfed, so one piece goes inside the other
pouring suggests a stream tumbling and splashing about, so the letters flow into a new order

parts.note: D is delta in the NATO alphabet
the letters of rain rearranged

explanation.surface: A river delta at its lowest ebb, flooded by heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the point directly below an observer, figuratively the worst or lowest moment.

clue.text: Deal with business matter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be about or relate to

explanation.surface: Handling a commercial affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' gives a third sense: a concern is also a matter of interest or worry.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to have as its subject, and the noun is a company or commercial enterprise.

clue.text: Judge in case of extreme perverted act gets matter thrown out

indicators.note: perverted means twisted out of its proper form, so the letters are distorted
in places one piece inside the other
the case of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are used

parts.note: the outer letters of extreme
J is the abbreviation for judge
the letters of act rearranged

explanation.surface: A judge hearing an extreme case of perversion orders material expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejecta is the material thrown out by a volcano or impact, a plural noun for expelled matter.

clue.text: Make good men, with return of last three, work suddenly

indicators.note: a return sends something back, so the final three letters of that word run backwards

parts.note: to atone is to make amends, or make good
fellows are men
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: An instruction to reform men and set them to work at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from Macbeth, means all at once in a single sudden action.

clue.text: Hostile takeover of company marred update and conclusion of contract

indicators.note: something marred is damaged, so the following word is spoilt into a new order

parts.note: standard abbreviation for company
the letters of update rearranged

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: final letter of contract

explanation.surface: A corporate story: a hostile bid spoilt by a software update and a contract's end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hostile takeover' reads as business jargon, but the definition is political: a seizure of government.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'état is a sudden, usually violent seizure of state power, a hostile takeover of a government.

clue.text: Person slow to appreciate some profound uncertainties

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: found spanning the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone who cannot grasp deep doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a slow learner, someone who struggles to understand things.

clue.text: Remove load from boat docked at noon

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a lighter is a flat-bottomed barge for unloading ships
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Unloading a vessel moored in the harbour at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' suggests a boat in harbour, but it means cut short: the barge loses its final R.
explanation.definitionFit: To lighten a ship or person is to reduce the weight carried, to take off part of the burden.

clue.text: Serious point about France regularly ignored

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a compass point

indicators.note: ignoring at regular intervals means every other letter is dropped and the rest kept

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of France

explanation.surface: A sober point made about France being routinely overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: The compass point is split open to take the kept letters inside it, rather than standing first.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means sincere and grave in intent, the opposite of joking, so it fits serious.

clue.text: Body temperature (approximately)

parts.note: standard abbreviation for temperature
'or so' means approximately

explanation.surface: A medical note: the body's temperature, roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the human body, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Making folio inscription attractive

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for folio
an etching is a design or text cut into a surface

explanation.surface: An engraved inscription on a folio page makes it look lovely.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching is an informal adjective for charming or good-looking.

clue.text: Unreported impact of success with career

parts.note: a hit is a success
with means together with, and
to career is to rush along, run

explanation.surface: A high-flying career whose successes went unreported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun for a working life but is the verb to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit-and-run is a collision where the driver flees without stopping or reporting it.

clue.text: New programmes supporting school spirit

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting means placed underneath, so those parts come after the other

parts.note: standard abbreviation for school
N is the abbreviation for new
apps are software programmes

explanation.surface: Fresh courses backing a school's ethos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School spirit' reads as morale; spirit alone is the definition, a strong drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong distilled alcoholic drink, a spirit, often flavoured with fruit.

clue.text: Terminate police officers found with crack

parts.note: DIs are Detective Inspectors
to crack a case is to solve it

explanation.surface: Detectives call time on a case once they have cracked it.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissolve a parliament, partnership or marriage is to bring it formally to an end.

clue.text: Humour is eluding cast

indicators.note: cast means thrown, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: the word supplies the letters

explanation.surface: Comedy that escapes the actors in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: To humour someone is to go along with their wishes, which is to indulge them.

clue.text: Mixer increasing the vibrancy of first note

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... water, added to spirits such as gin
second meaning: the keynote, first degree of a musical scale

explanation.surface: A drink mixer that livens up a scale's opening note.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle phrase hints at a third sense: a tonic is anything that invigorates.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic is both the carbonated quinine drink used in G&Ts and the musical name for the home note of a key.

clue.text: The New Yorker magazine's pages originally condemned Lolita?

indicators.note: something condemned is ruined, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
originally points to the opening letter of each word

parts.note: the opening letters of the four words
the letters of the word rearranged

explanation.surface: A literary magazine condemning Nabokov's notorious novel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags Lolita as an example: the novel's heroine is the archetype.
explanation.definitionFit: Nabokov's Humbert coins the word for a sexually precocious young girl, and Lolita is the type.

clue.text: Cast wanting week with good crowd

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter that stands for week is missing

parts.note: cast means thrown
W is the abbreviation for week
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A theatre cast lacking a week with a good audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large densely packed mass of people, a crowd.

clue.text: Time wasted in retreat's really not fair

indicators.note: something wasted is lost, so that letter disappears from inside the word

parts.note: a hideout is a hiding place or retreat, with the possessive s
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Wasting time in a retreat is grossly unjust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not fair' looks like a complaint about justice, but fair here means beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair can mean beautiful, so something very much not fair is extremely ugly.

clue.text: Group of players turned against boxing and suchlike

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards
boxing means enclosing, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: against, as in leaning one's back to the wall
etc, et cetera, means and suchlike

explanation.surface: A sports team that turned against boxing and similar sports.
explanation.definitionFit: An octet is a group of eight musicians, a set of players.

clue.text: Game in which bad play results in suspension?

definitions.text: Game in which bad play results in suspension?

parts.note: surface reading: foul play gets a sportsman banned

parts.words: Game in which bad play results in suspension?
parts.note: setter's reading: a pencil game where wrong guesses gradually draw a figure on a gallows

explanation.walkthrough: Suspension sounds like a ban from sport; in this word-guessing game it is a drawn figure hanging from a gibbet.
explanation.definitionFit: In the paper-and-pencil guessing game, each wrong letter adds a stroke to a drawing of an executed figure on a gibbet.

clue.text: New member of parliament initially offers women service of no use

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the next word only

parts.note: first letter of offers
W is the abbreviation for women
in tennis a let is a serve that does not count and is replayed

explanation.surface: A newly elected MP provides women with a useless service.
explanation.walkthrough: A group of owls is called a parliament, so its new member is a young owl, not a fresh politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Parliament is the collective noun for owls, and the young bird of that group is an owlet.

clue.text: People who allow joint possession

parts.note: to own is to admit or allow, so owners are people who allow
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: People who permit shared property rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint possession' reads as one legal phrase; joint belongs to the wordplay and possession alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of having legal title to something, i.e. possession of it.

clue.text: Large parrot that is mainly found in Africa

definitions.text: that is mainly found in Africa

parts.note: great means large
to parrot is to imitate, or ape

explanation.surface: A big parrot species found mostly in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parrot' looks like the bird, but it is the verb meaning to mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimpanzees and bonobos are African; only orangutans live in Asia, so this primate group is chiefly African.

clue.text: Makes one university publication for teachers

parts.note: short form of university
the TES, formerly the Times Educational Supplement, is a British weekly for teachers

explanation.surface: A university newspaper aimed at teaching staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite things is to join them together into a single whole.
